interest: These cross-reference sheets illustrate wartime Allied scrutiny of Irish neutrality and American anxiety over potential Axis espionage and surveillance networks operating out of Dublin. Although neutral Ireland was frequently suspected by Allied intelligence of harboring Axis operatives, the records reflect the Irish Legation's proactive effort to dispel rumors of a substantial Japanese intelligence footprint by emphasizing that only four Japanese nationals resided in the twenty-six counties. For diplomatic historians, they highlight high-level diplomatic exchanges between Under Secretary Sumner Welles and Irish Minister Robert Brennan, as well as the State Department's decimal filing practices for tracking Japanese intelligence and military activities across different geographic classifications.
overview: This file consists of two U.S. State Department cross-reference sheets from late November 1942 concerning the Japanese presence and potential Axis activities in Ireland during World War II. Cross-referencing communications originally filed under decimal files 800.202414/7 and 900.202414/8, the sheets record interactions between Irish Minister Robert Brennan and U.S. Under Secretary of State Sumner Welles. The underlying documents address inquiries regarding Axis intelligence gathering in neutral Ireland, noting specifically that only four Japanese nationals were present across the twenty-six counties and reviewing reports concerning Japanese tourists.

subfiles.summary: This State Department cross-reference sheet references an original paper dated November 23, 1942, from the Irish Legation filed under decimal number 800.202414/7. Concerning Axis agents in Ireland, it notes advice that there are only four Japanese in the twenty-six counties of Ireland. The reference is indexed under decimal file 894.202410/1 relating to Japanese military and intelligence activities.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Axis Agents in Ireland

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording a memorandum of conversation between Robert Brennan and Sumner Welles concerning Japanese tourists in Ireland.
subfiles.summary: This State Department cross-reference sheet indexes a memorandum of conversation dated November 25, 1942, between Irish Minister Robert Brennan and U.S. Under Secretary of State Sumner Welles. The underlying paper, filed under 900.202414/8, concerns discussions regarding Japanese tourists in Ireland. It is indexed under the State Department decimal classification for Japanese activities in Ireland.
